source.title: Inefficiency of K-FAC for Large Batch Size Training
source.authors: Linjian Ma; Gabe Montague; Jia-Yu Ye; Zhe-Wei Yao; A. Gholami; K. Keutzer; Michael W. Mahoney

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendix, is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests how batch size and training budget affect held-out performance and optimizer scaling, using K-FAC and SGD with an adjusted epoch budget and different measures from the version’s cited studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports batch-size effects on test accuracy, iterations to target test accuracy, and hyperparameter sensitivity. Numeric values for the principal batch-size comparisons appear only in figures; rows below record the authors’ textual descriptions without estimating plotted values. Cited findings from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study measures batch-size effects on held-out image-classification accuracy using adjusted epoch budgets, learning-rate schedule comparisons, and fixed-epoch accuracy distributions. These results test V5, including its dependence on the training recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. K-FAC provides comparable but not superior train/test performance under the tested training and tuning budgets, and has no better large-batch iteration scalability than SGD. Its hyperparameter robustness decreases with batch size under epoch budgets and increases under iteration budgets. The scaling metric excludes Fisher-matrix inversion cost.
record.recipe_differences: Uses K-FAC and SGD, batch-size sweeps, adjusted epoch budgets, scaled learning-rate schedules, and iteration-to-target measures; does not reproduce the fixed-epoch large-batch comparisons specified in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with batch size, epoch versus iteration budget, and fixed versus scaled learning-rate schedule. K-FAC hyperparameter robustness decreases with batch size under epoch budgets and increases with batch size under iteration budgets.

fits_no_version.finding: K-FAC and SGD exhibit diminishing iteration speedups to common reachable targets; K-FAC scales worse in the examined cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing batch size yields sublinear reductions in iterations to a common performance target, with K-FAC providing no scaling advantage over SGD in these workloads.

fits_no_version.finding: K-FAC hyperparameter robustness improves with batch size under fixed iteration budgets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relationship between batch size and hyperparameter robustness depends on whether training budgets fix epochs or iterations.

record.problems: The study’s epoch budget is adjusted upward with batch size, so its primary comparisons do not directly test fixed epoch budgets. The speedup measure ignores Fisher-matrix inversion cost. Numeric values for the principal comparisons are presented in figures rather than reported in the prose; no uncertainty estimates are stated.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive gradient methods versus SGD under limited tuning; K-FAC versus SGD with damping and momentum searches does not establish this comparison.

Language models, warmup, initial-learning-rate scaling, normalization or regularization interventions, and complete recovery of small-batch accuracy. Fixed-epoch distributions are reported for K-FAC, but the principal best-performance comparisons use batch-dependent epoch limits.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Matched-epoch K-FAC test-accuracy distributions: larger batches have lower distributions at a given stopping epoch, while longer training improves robustness. Record accuracy separately from hyperparameter sensitivity and training loss.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V5. A changed budget alone is not evidence against that version. Computational scaling and hyperparameter robustness should not be conflated with held-out accuracy. The supplied text supports qualitative directions but does not expose readable numerical curve values or uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD on held-out performance.

The study uses an adjusted epoch budget that extends epochs with batch size, not a fixed epoch budget. It does not test language models. It tests K-FAC and SGD, and compares learning-rate schedules for ResNet20.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

rows.subject: K-FAC
rows.operation_detail: Compared best test accuracy across batch sizes under an adjusted epoch budget and scaled learning-rate schedule.

conditions.value: ResNet20 and ResNet32 on CIFAR-10; AlexNet on SVHN

rows.measure: Best test accuracy versus batch size
rows.value: Authors state that larger batch sizes result in lower accuracies; K-FAC does not achieve higher accuracy than large-batch SGD given the same number of training epochs.
rows.note: The text describes the direction of the result but does not provide exact values. The budget extends epochs with batch size, so this is not a fixed-epoch comparison.
rows.check: The reported large-batch accuracy penalty is observed, not merely partial because the budget differs. Epoch limits increase with batch size, so this does not directly establish the fixed-epoch clause. K-FAC is an optimizer, not a model; separate the batch-size comparison from the K-FAC-versus-SGD comparison.

rows.subject: SGD
rows.operation_detail: Compared best test accuracy across batch sizes under an adjusted epoch budget and scaled learning-rate schedule.

conditions.value: ResNet20 and ResNet32 on CIFAR-10; AlexNet on SVHN

rows.measure: Best test accuracy versus batch size
rows.value: Authors state that best achieved accuracy drops for SGD beyond a certain batch size.
rows.note: The text states a drop beyond a certain batch size but does not identify a numeric threshold. The budget extends epochs with batch size.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports declining best accuracy beyond a batch-size threshold. The budget increases with batch size. SGD is an optimizer, not a model; Appendix A.3 specifically describes ResNet20, while Figure 1 covers all three workloads.

rows.subject: K-FAC
rows.operation_detail: Compared iterations to target test accuracy across batch sizes.

conditions.value: ResNet20 and ResNet32 on CIFAR-10; AlexNet on SVHN
test-accuracy thresholds selected to be reachable by all batch sizes

rows.measure: Iterations to target test accuracy; speedup relative to batch size 128
rows.baseline: Ideal scaling relationship between batch size and iterations
rows.value: Authors state that K-FAC deviates from ideal scaling more than SGD as batch size increases, with diminishing returns beginning immediately from the smallest batch size in the examined cases.
rows.note: The speedup measure counts iterations and ignores the cost of computing the Fisher-matrix inversion.
rows.check: Iterations to a deliberately reachable accuracy target measure computational efficiency, not a large-batch held-out performance penalty. Diminishing iteration speedup does not establish V5.

rows.subject: SGD
rows.operation_detail: Compared iterations to target test accuracy across batch sizes.

conditions.value: ResNet20 and ResNet32 on CIFAR-10; AlexNet on SVHN
test-accuracy thresholds selected to be reachable by all batch sizes

rows.measure: Iterations to target test accuracy; speedup relative to batch size 128
rows.baseline: Ideal scaling relationship between batch size and iterations
rows.value: Authors state that SGD also has diminishing returns as batch size increases, but deviates from ideal scaling less than K-FAC in all examined cases.
rows.check: Iterations to a common accuracy target measure computational efficiency rather than held-out performance differences under the budgets named by V5.

rows.subject: K-FAC
rows.operation_detail: Compared the spread of outcomes across 64 learning-rate and damping configurations at different batch sizes.

conditions.value: ResNet20 and ResNet32 on CIFAR-10; AlexNet on SVHN

rows.measure: Hyperparameter sensitivity of test accuracy and training loss
rows.baseline: Smaller batch sizes under the same adjusted-epoch-budget analysis
rows.value: Authors state that larger batch sizes produce lower accuracy and higher training loss that are more sensitive to hyperparameter choice.
rows.note: The hyperparameter spread is shown in figures and described in text; exact distribution values are not stated in prose.
rows.check: The lower test-accuracy distributions bear on V5; hyperparameter sensitivity and training loss alone do not. Split those measures. The adjusted epoch budget differs across batch sizes, and K-FAC is an optimizer.

rows.subject: K-FAC
rows.operation_detail: Compared outcomes across batch sizes at fixed hypothetical iteration budgets.
rows.measure: Hyperparameter robustness, assessed by test-accuracy and training-loss distributions
rows.baseline: Smaller batch sizes at the same iteration budget
rows.value: Authors state that robustness increases with larger batch size under iteration budgets, with large-batch distributions more concentrated toward higher accuracy and lower loss.
rows.note: The authors say the effect is less pronounced than for the fixed-epoch case.
rows.check: As framed, this row measures robustness across hyperparameter configurations under equal iteration budgets. It does not establish whether the large-batch accuracy penalty is reduced for comparably tuned models. The distribution shifts should not be treated as a reversal of V5.

rows.subject: SGD
rows.operation_detail: Compared fixed and scaled learning-rate decay schedules after separate hyperparameter searches.
rows.measure: Final test accuracy and training loss
rows.value: Authors state that the scaled schedule gives higher final test accuracy and lower final training loss across all batch sizes; the difference is more pronounced at large batch sizes, including 16K.
rows.note: Authors describe the schedule comparison but give no exact values in prose.
rows.check: The schedule improvement is explicitly observed. Fixed schedule means decays at epochs 40 and 80, not a fixed epoch budget or constant learning rate. Scaled schedule means decays at 40% and 80% of each adjusted training duration; it does not mean scaling the initial learning rate. No complete removal of the batch-size penalty is established.

rows.subject: K-FAC
rows.operation_detail: Compared fixed and scaled learning-rate decay schedules after separate hyperparameter searches.
rows.measure: Final test accuracy and training loss
rows.value: Authors state that the scaled schedule gives higher end-of-training accuracy and lower loss across all batch sizes.
rows.note: Authors characterize the scaled schedule as geared toward boosting large-batch scalability.
rows.check: The schedule improvement is explicitly observed. Specify delayed decay under the adjusted epoch budget; this is not an initial-learning-rate scaling or warmup experiment. Split test accuracy from training loss. K-FAC is an optimizer.

relationships.condition: K-FAC and SGD on the tested image workloads with adjusted epoch budgets and scaled decay schedules
relationships.reason: R1–R2 report a large-batch accuracy decline despite granting larger batches additional epochs; R5 also reports lower K-FAC accuracy distributions. This supports persistence of the penalty under this particular adapted recipe.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest larger batches retained accuracy deficits despite additional training epochs.

relationships.condition: K-FAC with ResNet20 on CIFAR-10 at matched stopping epochs
relationships.reason: The text accompanying Figure 4b explicitly reports lower test-accuracy distributions for larger batches at fixed epochs. This supports the fixed-epoch clause; the result is missing from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: The reported decline in test-accuracy distributions at matched epochs remains unverified for K-FAC, an optimizer that approximates loss curvature.

relationships.condition: ResNet20 on CIFAR-10, delayed versus fixed-epoch learning-rate decays
relationships.reason: R7–R8 report improved final test accuracy with delayed decays for both optimizers, especially at large batches for SGD, supporting recipe dependence without demonstrating elimination of the penalty.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest delayed learning-rate decay improved final accuracy, especially for large-batch SGD, without establishing complete recovery.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: Both methods show diminishing returns and batch-size-related test-performance loss, but the study grants larger batches additional epochs and selects reachable targets; R1–R4 therefore do not establish the version’s fixed-epoch claim directly.

reader_labels.reason: The scaled schedule improves final test accuracy and training loss across batch sizes, including a more pronounced difference at large batches, showing that schedule choice changes the outcome; R7–R8.
